title: Google's AI claimed Flock cameras hold $650 in gold and 23 pounds of copper — It was duped by meme
excerpt: The claim traces back to a joke that's been circulating for months among privacy activists, and Google’s AI Overview ran with it.
content_html:
Godwin Oluponmile

Sat, August 8, 2026 at 11:00 AM EDT 5 min read

As recently as Aug. 5, Google's AI was telling anyone who asked it that a Flock license plate camera reader holds up to 23 pounds of copper, plus several grams of gold — roughly $650.

The claim traces back to a joke that's been circulating for months. Flock's cameras, which photograph license plates and feed them into databases used by police, have a lot of enemies online.

Must Read

  • Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one

  • Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake. Here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP

  • Millionaires under 43 hold only 25% of their wealth in stocks. Here's where their money is actually going

Among privacy activists, a running gag took hold: there's supposedly a small fortune in metal inside each unit, so why not turn one into scrapyard money? It was a bit, not a tip. Google's AI didn't get the joke and started repeating it as fact. Adding to the mishap is the fact the Flock camera actually weighs about three pounds.

What the AI Overview said

Futurism's Joe Wilkins reported that if you searched "how much gold does a Flock camera have," Google gave you a straight answer. Each camera holds "about 1 to 5 grams of gold" in its circuit boards and wiring, the Overview claimed, along with as much as 23 pounds of copper. At that week's gold prices, 5 grams came to roughly $650 per camera.

And where did Google find all this? Two places. One was a Substack post from an anonymous account called "do.not.obey.do.not.comply," which put the scrap value at $150 to $500. Even that post didn't pretend to know — it said the figure came from "estimates based on scrap-value discussions," which is a long way of saying somebody guessed. The other source was an AI-generated Instagram post telling followers to tear into the hardware. The account behind it mostly posts about growing cannabis.

That was the entire evidence base behind an answer sitting in Google's most prominent slot, above every actual webpage.

Google didn't respond when Futurism reached out for comment. But by Aug. 6, when TechSpot's Skye Jacobs checked, the answer had flipped: the Overview now tells you the copper claim can't be true because the whole unit weighs about 3 pounds, that any gold is trace-level, and that the rumors "come from internet memes and AI hallucinations, not facts."

Which means a meme boosted by an AI-generated post, then repeated by Google's AI, is now being knocked down by the same AI that spread it.

content_html_zh:
戈德温·奥卢庞米尔

2026 年 8 月 8 日星期六，美国东部时间上午 11:00 阅读 5 分钟

就在 8 月 5 日，谷歌的人工智能告诉任何询问它的人，Flock 车牌摄像头读取器最多可容纳 23 磅铜，外加几克黄金——大约 650 美元。

这一说法可以追溯到一个流传了几个月的笑话。 Flock 的摄像头可以拍摄车牌并将其输入警方使用的数据库，但在网上却有很多敌人。

必读

  • 杰夫·贝索斯 (Jeff Bezos) 支持一个平台，让任何人都可以以低至 100 美元的价格投资出租房屋——无需真正成为房东即可像房东一样积累财富的 6 种方法
  • 戴夫·拉姆齐 (Dave Ramsey) 警告说，近 50% 的美国人正在犯一个重大的社会保障错误。 这就是它的本质以及尽快修复它的 3 个简单步骤
  • 43岁以下的百万富翁仅将其财富的25%投资于股票。 这就是他们的钱实际去向的地方

在隐私保护主义者中，流传着一个笑话：据说每个单元内都有一小笔金属，那么为什么不把其中的金属变成废品场的钱呢？ 这是一点，不是小费。 谷歌的人工智能没有理解这个笑话，并开始将其作为事实重复。 雪上加霜的是，Flock 相机实际上重约三磅。

人工智能概述说了什么

Futurism 的 Joe Wilkins 报道说，如果你搜索“Flock 相机有多少黄金”，谷歌会给你一个直接的答案。 概述称，每台相机的电路板和接线中都含有“约 1 至 5 克黄金”，以及多达 23 磅的铜。 按照那周的黄金价格计算，每台相机 5 克的价格约为 650 美元。

谷歌在哪里找到这一切？ 两个地方。 其中一个是来自名为“do.not.obey.do.not.comply”的匿名帐户的 Substack 帖子，该帖子将废品价值定为 150 至 500 美元。 就连那篇文章也没有假装知道——它说这个数字来自“基于废品价值讨论的估计”，这完全是有人猜测的。 另一个来源是人工智能生成的 Instagram 帖子，告诉粉丝撕碎硬件。 其背后的账户主要发布有关种植大麻的内容。

这就是谷歌最显眼的位置上答案背后的全部证据基础，位于每个实际网页的上方。

当未来主义联系谷歌发表评论时，谷歌没有回应。 但到了 8 月 6 日，当 TechSpot 的 Skye Jacobs 检查时，答案发生了翻转：概述现在告诉你铜的说法不可能是真的，因为整个单位重约 3 磅，任何黄金都是微量级的，而且谣言“来自互联网模因和人工智能幻觉，而不是事实”。

这意味着由人工智能生成的帖子推动的模因，然后由谷歌的人工智能重复，现在正被传播它的同一个人工智能击倒。
